note: F-0490 = UsageMetric.TRACKED_CREATOR. F-0506 = the three CreatorMetric avg* fields. F-0525 = AdminSupportService.avgResponseTime (caught by RULE 3, added this task). F-0689 = MediaMetric.avgWatchTimeSeconds. F-0688 (UsageMetric.EXPORT) was already deleted from the enum before this baseline was recorded and will never appear in a live scan again; it stays named in the gate's header per RETENTION rule 3. UsageMetric.CREATOR_ANALYTICS_VIEW was listed here earlier today as a claimed 'real, live 6th instance' -- that claim was FALSE and has been retracted (T-DEADMETRIC-0913 closing round). It is a scanner artifact, not a defect: RULE 1's literal-proximity check only ever looks for `UsageMetric.CONST` sitting near a write-shaped call, and this constant is never itself a write-call argument -- it is returned from EntitlementService.meteredMetricFor, bound to a local (`metric`) in EntitlementService.consume, and THAT local is what reaches usageCounterService.incrementUsage (EntitlementService.java:147, the unlimited/Pro branch) and usageCounterService.recordCreatorLookup (EntitlementService.java:150 -> UsageCounterService.java:149 via incrementUsageForPeriod, the capped branch). Both call paths were opened and traced by hand before this note was written. RULE 1 now follows exactly one local-variable hop (direct assignment, or a local bound to a method's return value) and correctly reports this metric as written; TRACKED_CREATOR, which is never bound to a local at all, is unaffected and still reports dead. This baseline is a ratchet CEILING: the live set must stay a SUBSET of this list. It may fall as metrics get real writers (lower the list when that happens) and must never silently grow -- a metric appearing here that is not in this list means the gate goes RED. A metric REMOVED from this baseline because it was wrongly added (not because it was fixed) is not a 'SHRUNK' event in the ordinary sense -- it is a baseline correction, recorded here rather than silently dropped. T-DEADMETRIC-REPAIR-0915 (2026-09-15) closed 5 of the original 6: CreatorMetric.avgEngagementRate/avgReachPerPost/avgImpressionsPerPost (F-0506) now have a real writer -- MetricsPollingJob.pollOne aggregates them from this same poll's media_metrics rows via the new averageOf/averageEngagementRate helpers, proven by a falsified-and-restored test (MetricsPollingJobTest). AdminSupportService.avgResponseTime (F-0525) now has a real writer too -- computeAvgResponseTimeHours() derives time-to-first-admin-reply from SupportTicketMessage (senderType=ADMIN, createdAt), no new column needed, proven the same way (AdminSupportServiceTest). MediaMetric.avgWatchTimeSeconds (F-0689) was REMOVED entirely (field, getter, builder method, and the AnalyticsDtos.ContentPerformanceResponse field that surfaced it) rather than repaired -- Meta was never asked for a watch-time insight metric, so there was no real data to aggregate; inventing one would fabricate a measurement, which is the defect class this gate exists to catch, not fix. Its DB column (V21) is left in place, unmapped, for a live-MySQL-verified drop later. UsageMetric.TRACKED_CREATOR (F-0490) is the one entry still here ON PURPOSE: its only plausible writer is the saved-creator cap (SM-2.2 / lane item C1), a separate, not-yet-built assignment -- wiring an increment here with no enforcement behind it would be worse than leaving it honestly dead.
